tour.title: Central Agent Orchestrator
tour.description: Start with REEAgent, the ~11.8k-line top-level module that assembles every subsystem into a single cognitive loop. AgentState holds the mutable per-tick fields (latents, drives, goal, residues) that flow between modules, while REEConfig gathers the 16 subsystem configs (~674 knobs) that parameterise the whole substrate. Reading these two files first gives you the vocabulary for every later step.
tour.languageLesson: REEConfig uses a nested dataclass tree — a common Python pattern for large, versioned configuration surfaces. Sub-configs (e.g. E3Config, SleepConfig) compose into REEConfig, so a single frozen instance carries the full substrate contract; version_layering.py then enforces that V4/V5 flags stay off unless the architecture epoch permits them.

tour.title: Environment: CausalGridWorld
tour.description: Every REEAgent tick begins with an observation from CausalGridWorld — a 2D grid world with causal object rules that supplies observations, actions, and rewards. Understanding the observation shape and reward structure here anchors what the perception and prediction stacks (Steps 3–4) are actually consuming.

tour.title: Latent Stack: z_self, z_world, z_harm
tour.description: The latent stack encodes raw observations into the split latent spaces (z_self body-state, z_world external state, z_harm harm streams, z_goal, z_block) that every downstream module consumes. SelfRecurrence gives z_self temporal depth so 'who I am' persists across ticks, and ThetaBuffer time-averages latents on the theta rhythm so E3 can score trajectories against a coherent temporal window. This is where the brain-region-named modules first attach to the environment from Step 2.

tour.title: Predictors: E1, E2, and E3
tour.description: REE is a three-timescale prediction hierarchy. E1 is the long-horizon deep predictor (LSTM over latent state), E2 is the fast single-step forward model of both self and world (plus its counterfactual and harm variants), and E3 is the slow deliberative trajectory selector that scores candidate rollouts and drives action selection. Together they implement the perception -> prediction -> selection backbone that the rest of the substrate modulates.
tour.languageLesson: E2 uses residual-delta prediction (predict the change, not the next state) — a common PyTorch pattern for forward-model stability that keeps gradients well-scaled and prevents the model from having to relearn identity every step.

tour.title: Hippocampal Memory and Residue Field
tour.description: Long-horizon behaviour needs memory. The hippocampal module composes a scale-tagged anchor store, an event segmenter that carves experience into segments, and a ghost-goal bank that scores anchors on a wanting+goal-match+staleness ranking. The residue field (an RBF layer) maintains a distributed valence/care-marker memory over z_world, and the object-file buffer keeps per-entity persistence across ticks — together giving the agent 'this place matters', 'that object is the same one', and 'I still want the thing from earlier'.

tour.title: Cingulate and Salience Coordinator
tour.description: The cingulate cluster (SD-032) drives adaptive control on top of the E-stack. dACC computes precision-weighted affective control signals, AIC codes interoceptive urgency, pACC integrates sustained affective pain, and PCC emits a stability parameter. The salience coordinator aggregates that dACC bundle with homeostatic and offline signals into the arbitration signal that decides which stream gets write access and which mode the agent is in.

tour.title: PFC Analogs: Rules, Outcomes, and Escape
tour.description: The PFC analogs sit above the cingulate arbitration from Step 6. Lateral PFC holds gate-modulated EMA rule/goal state, OFC provides state-code and score-bias heads that inject outcome value into E3, the escape-affordance bridge binds actions to relief/safety so the agent can act instrumentally under threat, and the frontopolar analog (BA10, V4-scope) reserves the metacognitive de-commit lever. This is where deliberation and rule-following live.

tour.title: Policy, Candidate Rules, and Goal
tour.description: The policy layer converts the deliberated E3 scores from Step 4 into an action. z_goal is a slow-decay attractor in z_world space that gives the agent something to persist toward. The candidate rule field mints structurally distinct rule proposals; the gated policy scores them with two symmetry-broken heads; structured curiosity adds a novelty+uncertainty bonus on top. This is the last hop before the environment.

tour.title: Regulators, Amygdala, and Neuromodulation
tour.description: Homeostatic control wraps around the E-stack and policy layer. GABAergic decay applies tonic cross-stream decay so nothing runs away, BLA/CeA (amygdala analogs) supply threat evaluation and rapid defensive prediction, and the serotonin module maintains tonic 5-HT with phase-dependent benefit/harm salience tagging. These are the slow modulators that make the substrate stable across many ticks and set the affective 'weather' the deliberative layers operate under.

tour.title: Sleep, Consolidation, and Closure
tour.description: Waking is only half the loop. The sleep package runs SWS/REM phases via a deterministic K-episode driver; the replay sampler draws anchors from Step 5 by staleness/priority; the Bayesian aggregator writes per-domain per-region Gaussian posteriors back into the substrate; and the closure operator (SD-034) emits the coordinated five-part 'done' token that releases the beta-gate and lets the next episode begin. This is where learning across episodes actually happens.

tour.title: Coordinator: HTTP Service and Sync Daemon
tour.description: REE runs across a fleet (hub + cloud workers), and the coordinator is the fleet's brain. app.py is a stdlib http.server exposing /claim, /result, /heartbeat, /status; db.py is the SQLite store and the authoritative claim arbiter; sync_daemon.py runs the Phase-3 writers that materialise result manifests, the queue snapshot, and heartbeat/status telemetry back into git — under an active-claim guard that blocks a writer while a session holds the same path. manifest_spool.py is the crash-safe on-disk queue between /result POSTs and the git writer.
tour.languageLesson: The coordinator deliberately uses only the Python stdlib (http.server, sqlite3, threading) — no Flask, no SQLAlchemy. This 'boring stack' choice makes the service auditable and dependency-free on every worker, which matters when the whole fleet must agree on claim state under partial network failures.

tour.title: Coordinator Data Model and Operator Docs
tour.description: The coordinator's SQLite schema defines five tables — experiments (the queue), results (manifest bytes as BLOB), heartbeats (per-machine liveness), commands (remote-control channel), and claim_log (append-only diagnostic ledger) — plus partial indexes for pending-command and diverged-claim lookups. PLAN.md is the plan-of-record for what the service is and why; PHASE3_CUTOVER.md documents the env knobs and writer behaviour of the current live phase; OPERATOR_GUIDE.md is what an operator reads to run the system day-to-day. These artifacts close the loop between the code in Step 11 and the fleet actually running experiments.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite partial indexes (e.g. idx_commands_pending WHERE acked_at IS NULL) index only the rows matching a predicate — orders of magnitude smaller than a full-column index when the hot query is 'give me all pending things'. The commands and claim_log tables both use this pattern to keep polling cheap as the log grows.
